about: The Ave Regina Caelorum is the final Marian antiphon for the season from the Purification of the Blessed Virgin Mary into Holy Week. In successive salutations the faithful call Mary Queen of the heavens, Lady of the Angels, the root and gate from whom the Light arose for the world, and finally ask her to intercede with Christ.

w001.function: The imperative serves as the first salutation addressed to Mary.

w002.function: The vocative addresses Mary as Queen.

w004.function: The repeated “Ave” opens the parallel second salutation.

w005.function: The vocative is a second title of Mary.

w006.function: The genitive depends on “Dómina” and calls her Lady of the Angels.

w007.function: The first “Salve” greets Mary under the image of a root.

w008.function: The metaphorical vocative addresses Mary as the root from which the saving Light springs.

w009.function: The repeated verb introduces the second parallel image.

w010.function: The metaphorical vocative calls Mary the gate through which the Light came into the world.

w011.function: The preposition with the ablative marks origin: the Light arose from Mary represented as the gate.

w012.function: The ablative relative refers to Mary, immediately named “porta”.

w013.function: A dative of advantage or reference: the Light arose for the world.

w014.function: The nominative is the subject of “orta est”. The Light denotes Christ.

w015.function: With “orta” it forms the deponent perfect: “arose”.

w016.function: The perfect participle of a deponent verb agrees with “lux” and with “est” forms the past-tense predicate.

w017.function: The imperative calls Mary to rejoice.

w018.function: The vocative names the addressee again.

w020.function: The preposition with the accusative introduces the range surpassed.

w021.function: The feminine adjective is used substantively: Mary is beautiful above all women or virgins.

w022.function: The substantival vocative adjective describes Mary as beautiful above all.

w023.function: The imperative “be well” functions here as a farewell, distinct from the earlier “Ave” and “Salve”.

w026.function: The substantival vocative adjective describes Mary as comely and graceful. It remains distinct from “speciósa”.

w028.function: The preposition with the ablative identifies those on whose behalf Mary is to ask.

w029.function: The ablative after “pro” includes the worshipers who speak.

w030.function: The accusative names the person Mary is to entreat, not the thing requested.

w031.function: The final imperative asks Mary to entreat Christ on behalf of the faithful.
